title: [14] Integrate Metered.ca TURN server and make ICE config dynamic
why_we_need_this: Video calls fail for users behind restrictive NATs (e.g. Russian ISPs) because: (1) the only configured STUN servers are Google's (stun.l.google.com), which are blocked/unreliable in Russia; (2) TURN_SERVER_URL is empty — no relay fallback exists; (3) ICE servers are hardcoded in frontend/services/webrtc.ts and ignore backend TURN config entirely. Without a working TURN relay, calls cannot connect when direct/STUN paths are blocked.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Backend exposes ICE server list dynamically: a new endpoint GET /calls/ice-servers (or include in WebSocket call_initiated/incoming_call payloads) returns the full ICE server array built from STUN_SERVERS + TURN env vars in config.py
2. Frontend fetches ICE servers from backend instead of using the hardcoded list in @frontend/services/webrtc.ts — the hardcoded Google STUN fallback remains only if the backend is unreachable
3. Replace default Google STUN servers with Metered.ca STUN+TURN URLs in production env vars (STUN_SERVERS, TURN_SERVER_URL, TURN_SERVER_USERNAME, TURN_SERVER_CREDENTIAL)
4. TURN config includes both UDP and TCP/TLS (port 443) transports so traffic passes through firewalls that block non-HTTPS ports
5. Calls connect successfully when both peers are behind symmetric NAT (TURN relay path works end-to-end)
6. Existing call flow (direct/STUN path) still works — no regression for users with open connectivity
7. .env.example updated with Metered.ca placeholder values and comments explaining each TURN variable
8. All platforms (web, iOS, Android) receive and use the dynamic ICE config
important_constraints:
- Do NOT hardcode Metered.ca credentials in source code — env vars only
- TURN TCP/443 (TURNS) transport is mandatory, not optional — it's the only transport that reliably passes through corporate/ISP firewalls
- ICE server list must include both STUN and TURN entries; TURN alone is not enough (wastes relay bandwidth when direct path works)
- Frontend must handle the case where backend ICE endpoint is unavailable — fall back to hardcoded STUN (non-Google, e.g. Metered.ca free STUN)
- Keep backward compatibility: if TURN env vars are empty, system works as before (STUN only)
